author: janleike
text: @jonathanstray @Miles_Brundage @jachiam0 @AmandaAskell Other examples are GANs and GAIL where your training signal comes out of a neural network. Not sure how much they are "in deployment" today, though it wouldn't be hard to imagine that Photoshop ships with some generative image models in a few years.

author: janleike
text: @jonathanstray @Miles_Brundage @jachiam0 @AmandaAskell But this is relevant for industrial robotics tasks today, e.g. if you're trying to insert deformable clips on a factory belt. See e.g. this paper, where they learn a reward function from images: https://t.co/AcLhAYDdpV

author: janleike
text: @jonathanstray @Miles_Brundage @jachiam0 @AmandaAskell How would you do this without using ML? Maybe doable in sim, but with a real robot...?

author: janleike
text: @jonathanstray @Miles_Brundage @jachiam0 @AmandaAskell How would you hardcode an objective function for a task that is just not simple to evaluate procedurally? E.g. if I want to train a robot with RL to arrange some blocks in a circle?
